articles.description:
I am a local civil servant at the Gwangjin-gu District Office in Seoul. I spent seven years wrestling HWP files at work, and when I started wiring LLMs into that work, the files were the first wall I hit. Almost everything I read and write on the job is an HWP or HWPX document. RAG pipelines and AI agents want Markdown. So I built kordoc, an MIT-licensed TypeScript library, CLI and MCP server that converts Korean documents into Markdown and structured data.
HWP is the Hancom word processor format, and there is more than one of it:
HWP 5.x is an OLE2 compound file (CFB). The body is a series of records, zlib-compressed, with text in UTF-16LE. For damaged files, kordoc includes a lenient CFB recovery parser ported from rhwp.
HWPX is a ZIP archive of XML: section XML for the body, head.xml fo…

articles.author: Samson JK
articles.description:
Hey DEV 👋
I’ve been building ActionNote.io, an AI meeting summarizer designed to turn meeting conversations into something people can actually use afterward.
The problem I’m trying to solve is simple:
A meeting ends, and everyone remembers the discussion differently.
Then come the usual questions:
What exactly did we decide?
What are the action items?
Who owns each action?
What is still unresolved?
What needs to be followed up?
Most meeting tools can generate transcripts and summaries.
With ActionNote, I’m exploring something slightly more structured:
Meeting → Summary → Decisions → Action Items → Owners → Follow-up
The goal is to turn a meeting into clear, actionable notes instead of just producing another block of AI-generated text.
ActionNote currently focuses on extracting things such as:
Key discussion points
Meeting summary
Decisions made
Action items
Owners
Important insights
Risks or unresolved items
Follow-up topics
It’s still an early version, and this is exactly the stage where I want real feedback before building too much around assumptions.
So I’m looking for people who are willing to try it with an actual meeting.
👉 Try ActionNote: https://actionnote.io
I’d especially love feedback on these three questions:
What did ActionNote capture well?
What important information did it miss or misunderstand?
Would you actually use this output after a meeting?
If the answer to the third question is no, I’d love to know why.
That feedback is probably more valuable to me right now than adding another feature.
Thanks to anyone willing to try it and share feedback.


  
  
  ai #buildinpublic #productivity #saas #meetings
articles.title: Building ActionNote.io — an AI Meeting Summarizer Focused on Actions, Not Just Summaries

articles.description:
Short answer: curl: (60) means one thing only: the peer's certificate did not verify. Everything after the colon is written by whichever TLS library curl was compiled against, so Peer certificate cannot be authenticated with known CA certificates, SSL certificate problem: self-signed certificate in certificate chain and SSL certificate verification failed: certificate signer not trusted can all be the same broken trust store on three different boxes. Run curl -V before you search for the message, because the message identifies the build and not the fault.
Fix: read curl -V first. The backend name in that line decides how every TLS failure will be phrased, and searching the phrase without it sends you to answers written for a different library.
Detail: error 60 is CURLE_PEER_FAILED_VERIFICA…
